# Medicus SOP This is the list of procedures, responsibilities, and duties of the [color=#42636d][bold]Medicus[/bold][/color] of this station.
The Medicus is a senior role to all other [color=#42636d][bold]Medical[/bold][/color] personnel except the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color].
When selecting an Acting CMO, the Medicus should be considered above all other Medical staff. Should the CMO become incapacitated, the Medicus should assume the role of acting head as soon as is convenient for the situation. The Medicus as an acting head will fully assume the associated responsibilities, including ensuring the efficacy of the department as a whole instead of solely focusing on training.
The Medicus shares all responsibilities of other Medical staff but is to prioritize training, directing, and advising their staff, even during station-threatening events. To this end, the appropriate role's SOP should be consulted depending on whom the Medicus instructs. Mind that the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Chief Medical Officer[/bold][/color]'s orders are final on how the department will operate and what orders must be followed. Failure to perform these priorities or to act as a role model is grounds for demotion.
1. The Medicus is expected to instruct [color=#42636d][bold]Medical Interns[/bold][/color] on how to perform their duties and to guide other Medical personnel should they ask for help. [bold]Interns are to be prioritized first[/bold], but should the intern decline help, the Medicus does not need to focus their attention on them. The Medicus should be open-minded to all available methods when teaching staff, even if it may not be the most familiar to the Medicus.
2. The Medicus is expected to fulfill the duties of other Medical personnel [bold]if and only if[/bold] there are no Medical Interns needing to be instructed. In addition, when assuming other duties, the Medicus is expected to follow the same SOP as the role they will perform.
3. The Medicus is expected to have a comprehensive understanding of the SOP and duties of each departmental role and may be consulted at any time regarding proper procedure. Additionally, the Medicus must ensure their department is following SOP and is expected to remind staff and/or the department head to do so.
4. The Medicus should be clearly distinguishable from other staff of their department, meaning that they ought to wear the appropriately designated clothing for their role. Consequently, the Medicus should not give to other personnel any Nanotrasen property assigned to them except for instructional use or in case of station-threatening emergency.
5. The Medicus is permitted to acquire surplus equipment and apparel of their department explicitly for training purposes.
6. The Medicus may ask certain departmental personnel to vacate equipment for the sake of training. However, this request may be refused if there is an urgent need or if it would be unwise to vacate at that moment. Unreasonable refusal to vacate is grounds for disciplinary action should the department head find it necessary.
7. The Medicus is [bold]not[/bold] entitled to sit in on a [color=#42636d][bold]Psychologist[/bold][/color]'s meeting with a client. Should the Psychologist request assistance, the Medicus may enter the meeting space, but the Medicus is not entitled to linger once the meeting resumes.
